sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 461.5 ± 28.6 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Co-immunoprecipitation and western blot confirmed expression of Xpress-H3R; BRET signal detected between Xpress-H3R and H3R-YFP, indicating receptor dimerization is preserved. Canonical H3R ligand-binding or G-protein signaling was NOT MEASURED for the tagged construct specifically.
sites.rationale: H3R has no endogenous signal peptide (EC1 begins at Met1 per the topology landmarks), so an N-terminal tag prepends before residue 1 (insert_after_residue=0, residue_after=M). This is the sole extracellular terminus available for an N-terminal tag on this seven-TM GPCR, making the position topology_derived. The same junction is independently supported by L2 (FLAG+8×His with exogenous bovine prolactin SP in Sf9 cells), L3 (BN NanoBiT at N-terminus in Sf9), L7 (same Xpress construct as L6), and L11 (FLAG tag in purification construct); L6 is chosen as the primary clip because it demonstrates mammalian-cell surface expression with co-IP and BRET readout. Python confirmed residue 1 = M. HEK293 cells co-transfected with Xpress-H3R (N-terminal Xpress epitope tag) and H3R-YFP (C-terminal YFP); both constructs expressed and detected by co-immunoprecipitation and western blot in a BRET-based receptor dimerization study. The N-terminus of H3R (EC1: residues 1–34) is extracellular per topology; no endogenous signal peptide is present, so the tag prepends directly before Met1. No specific residue number is named in the paper, but the N-terminus is the only extracellular terminus available for an N-terminal tag on this GPCR.

sources.claim: HEK293 cells were co-transfected with two different H 3 R constructs, H 3 R-YFP and Xpress-H 3 R, expressing the receptor tagged at its N-terminus with an Xpress epitope.

literature_notes: Five ledger lines (L2, L3, L6, L7, L11) all independently support an N-terminal extracellular tag on full-length H3R; they converge on the same single junction (prepend before Met1) and are therefore one site, not five. L1 reports a HaloTag substitution spanning IL3 residues Arg230–Arg347, which falls entirely within the intracellular IC3 loop (topology: 223–359) and is recorded in other_positions. L4 (LgBiT), L5 (YFP/RLuc), L8/L9/L10 (GFP), and the C-terminal MBP of L11 are all C-terminal fusions; the C-terminus of H3R is intracellular (IC4: 416–445) and these are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line reports any insertion in an extracellular loop (ECL1 93–108, ECL2 175–196, ECL3 381–395), so no internal extracellular sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: HaloTag substituted into IL3 from Arg230 to Arg347 (IC3: 223–359 per topology) as part of a NanoBRET conformational biosensor; entirely intracellular, not a surface tag site.
LgBiT fused directly to the C-terminus of H3R (after residue 445); the C-terminus lies in IC4 (416–445) and is intracellular.
C-terminal YFP and RLuc fusions to H3R used for BRET dimerization studies; C-terminus is intracellular (IC4: 416–445).
C-terminal GFP fusion (H3R_FL-GFP and H3R_i3d-GFP) expressed in yeast; C-terminus is intracellular (IC4: 416–445).
